title: R’ Yehoshua bar Zidal
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman relates from Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3 and Avodah Zarah 2:3 that R’ Yehoshua bar Zidal fell ill. Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Hoshaya (b), Rabbi Bun bar Kahana and Rabbi Chananyah, a colleague of the Rabbis, came to visit him. (Hyman says Avodah Zarah mistakenly reads R’ Yehoshua in place of Hoshaya, and Terumot omits “a colleague of the Rabbis.”) They sat and said: “Here is the authority for the teaching, and here is the man involved in the incident.” Hyman says he is not mentioned elsewhere.

notes.text: The checked Avodah Zarah passage makes Rabbi Yannai son of Rabbi Yishmael the sick man; Rabbi Yehoshua bar Zaidal is already sitting there when the visitors arrive. Hyman’s different account is retained as a source question. His Hoshaya/Yehoshua variant and the unmatched footnote marker (b) are preserved.

The saved whole Venice Terumot 8 scalar [2][3] has full Rabbi Yannai son of Rabbi Yishmael as the sick man, with Yehoshua bar Zidal already seated there. It also INCLUDES Chananyah’s חברהון דרבנין, contrary to Hyman’s reported omission. The named paragraph supports full Rabbi for these inspected visitor occurrences, not the abbreviated local heading or every catalog occurrence. The earlier Avodah Zarah comparison is inherited, not newly inspected. Hyman’s Hoshaya/Yehoshua mistake claim and statement that the subject is nowhere else mentioned remain attributed, not fresh corpus-wide findings. The unmatched ב) marker and uncertain referents of authority/incident remain; no footnote or identity is invented.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume II, printed p. 623, retains the notice’s compressed sick-man account, the Hoshaya/Yehoshua comparison, and the reported omission of “colleague of the Rabbis.” In the printed line, ר׳ הושעיא ב is grouped in parentheses; the isolated ב) in the supplied transcription is not supplemented with invented footnote text. The whole consulted Venice Terumot paragraph makes Yannai son of Yishmael ill, with Yehoshua bar Zidal already seated, and includes Chananyah’s colleague phrase. The whole consulted Guggenheimer Avodah Zarah 2:3 paragraph likewise makes Yannai ill; its Hebrew has Yehoshua among the visitors, while its English explicitly offers (Joshua) [Hoshaia] using the Terumot comparison. Hyman’s different account and his statement that the subject occurs nowhere else remain attributed claims, not fresh corpus-wide findings. No new person or authority identity follows from these variants.
